historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Purvi was an ancient name for the eastern direction in Hindu culture. The name Purvi carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Indian subcontinent has six directions - north (Uttar), east (Purvi), south (Dakshin), west (Pravah), north-east (Agneya), and south-east (Nabhasa) - which are personified as gods. Purvi was the goddess of the eastern direction.

historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, Purvi was also the name of the daughter of the sage Vedavyasa and his wife Satyavati. She was the mother of the legendary king Vyasa, who is believed to be the author of the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.
historical_references.context: Vedavyasa, being a great sage and scholar, was tasked with the mission of recording the epic tales of the Indian subcontinent. To fulfill his mission, he had to have children who would become the protagonists of these tales. Purvi, being his wife, gave birth to the legendary king Vyasa, who went on to pen down the two most revered texts of Hinduism - the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.
